inline_text:
## Purpose

Adds four candidate terms, with proposed definitions, covering the supply chain of agent tools (for example MCP servers and their tool definitions). They are the terms an agent operator needs in order to talk about a tool that is malicious from day one, a tool that turns malicious after it was approved, how to check a tool definition before use, and data crossing between clients of a shared tool server.

Terms added (`taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js`, new section "Security & Privacy — agent tool supply chain", one commit per term):

- Tool poisoning
- Rug pull
- Tool definition verification (alias: Tools manifest verification)
- Cross-client data leakage

A fifth candidate, "Tool description ambiguity", was dropped before this PR was opened: it had no authoritative external source defining it as agent-specific (materially different from ordinary ambiguous API documentation), which is the workstream's own bar for inclusion. Happy to reintroduce it in a follow-up if a Domain Editor thinks it clears that bar.

## Working groups affected

| Term | workgroups |
|---|---|
| Tool poisoning | Security & Privacy; Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment |
| Rug pull | Security & Privacy; Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment |
| Tool definition verification | Security & Privacy; Identity & Trust |
| Cross-client data leakage | Security & Privacy; Identity & Trust |

## Schema and conventions

- `category` is `''` and `broaderTerm` is `null`, per the deferred-field convention in `docs/data-schemas.md`.
- `relatedTerms` / `contrastsWith` reference only terms that already exist in `main` (`Attestation`, `Session`) or are added in this same PR.
- Paired-contrast rule (CONTRIBUTING 5.C.2): Tool poisoning vs. Rug pull (what is manipulated vs. when it changes), Tool definition verification vs. Attestation (checking a claim vs. making one).
- Definitions are vendor-neutral and name no product or member organization. The one exception, an npm package name and CVE/GHSA ID in a security advisory citation, names an upstream open-source SDK component (not an AAIF member or product) and is cited by ID only, consistent with the embargo/vendor-neutral rules.
- External references were fetched and verified directly against primary sources, not carried over from memory: MITRE ATLAS (`atlas-data` `main`, AML.T0109 "AI Supply Chain Rug Pull", AML.T0110 "AI Agent Tool Poisoning"), OWASP MCP Top 10 (2025) MCP03/MCP04/MCP10, CoSAI "Model Context Protocol (MCP) Security" draft dated 8 January 2026, GHSA-345p-7cg4-v4c7 / CVE-2026-25536 (via `gh api`).

## Notes for reviewers

- Note: Typosquatting (Spreadsheet Row 34) is marked `CULL` in the working document and is not addressed in this PR. It is also not present in `taxonomy/taxonomy-data.js` on `main`, and no open PR or issue adds it.
- **Definitions are proposals**, in the same style as merged PRs #59 and #60. `docs/data-schemas.md` still documents a pending-placeholder convention for an admit-first/define-later pass, but recent merged PRs shipped real definitions directly, so this PR follows that now-established practice rather than the placeholder.
- **None of these four terms is in the working spreadsheet's Keep/Cull list**, unlike every other merged definition PR in this repository's history (#56, #59, #60 all defined terms the spreadsheet had already marked Keep). This is a process deviation — happy to move the spreadsheet entries first if that's the preferred order; drafted rows are in this branch's working notes and can be posted on request.
- **Tool poisoning and Rug pull each lead with the material-difference test** the workstream itself applies (per `ONBOARDING.md` sec. 3): what makes the agent-specific mechanism different from the pre-existing general-security concept, not just a restatement of it.
- **One commit per term.** Any term can be removed independently via `git revert <sha>` (in reverse commit order for the tail) without touching the others.

Requested reviewers (Security & Privacy Domain Editors): Katherine Druckman (@kdruckman); Domain Editors from Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment (@kjamithash), and/or Identity & Trust (@julianna-ciq) for cross-WG approval.
